ModMetadata.Name: ScriptedScreens Vector [StationeersLaunchPad]
ModMetadata.Author: Gruffuss
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]ScriptedScreens Vector[/h1] [i]Client-side only. Nothing on disk is modified.[/i]
Adds a [b]vector[/b] element type to ScriptedScreens surfaces. Instead of drawing pixel by pixel onto a canvas, you describe a picture once and the game draws it as real geometry — then animates it on your machine, every frame, for free.
[h2]Why you want it[/h2] A canvas console costs roughly [b]10 FPS[/b], and the cause is the number of drawing operations per frame. Every one is recorded, batched, sent over the network, replayed, and uploaded as a texture — sixty times a second.
This makes that count [b]zero[/b]. The scene is sent once. Movement is described with expressions and evaluated on the client, so an animated console needs no per-frame Lua and no per-frame network traffic.
Tessellation runs on a worker thread. A console with 800 shapes animating at 30 Hz costs about [b]0.4% of a frame[/b] on the main thread — a console being switched on is not measurably different from it being off.
[h2]What you can draw[/h2] [list] [*] Rectangles with real rounded corners, ellipses, polygons, SVG paths with holes [*] Smooth liquid surfaces, waveforms and area charts that read as continuous edges [*] Catmull-Rom splines, strokes with caps, joins and dashes [*] Linear, radial and conic gradients, including ones that follow the shape they fill [*] Real alpha — no more pre-composited opaque palettes [*] Antialiased edges, sized in screen pixels so they look right at any distance [*] Clipping to any outline, so a liquid stays in its tank [*] Pictures from a URL, drawn in scene order [*] CSS colour filters, gradient masks and matrix transforms on groups [*] Opacity ramps along a surface, for gas fades that follow a moving edge [*] Soft drop shadows and inner shadows, evaluated analytically -- no offscreen pass [*] Text that moves, scales, rotates and scrolls with the artwork, in any font the game has [*] Scrolling containers for lists longer than the console -- the wheel costs the chip nothing [*] Clickable nodes, so a row of tiles no longer needs a transparent button over every one [*] Reusable symbols: write a row or a lamp once, stamp it with different parameters [/list]
[h2]How it animates[/h2] Any number can be an expression over [b]t[/b] (time), [b]i[/b] (repeat index) and your own data values:
[code]{ op = "R", x = 10, y = "=100-$fill*100", h = "=$fill*100", f = "#2E8B6E" }[/code]
Send [i]fill[/i] twice a second and the bar moves smoothly at display rate. Values are eased between updates automatically, so a gauge never steps.
[b]hash(i)[/b] gives each instance of a repeat stable pseudo-random values, identical on every client with nothing transmitted — which is what makes a 400-mote particle field cost one node instead of four hundred.
[h2]A scene can be written as text[/h2] Instead of nested Lua tables, one node per line:
[code]R x=10 y=10 w=44 h=60 rx=8 f=#0B1622 G clip=tank { YS n=24 x==8+i*1.75 y==64-$fill*52 y2=72 f=@liquid }[/code]
A static layout written this way is a string literal, already in the compiled script, so it costs the chip nothing to build. A generated one costs about what the tables cost -- this is a way to write a screen, not a way to buy back your instruction budget.
[h2]Resolution independent[/h2] Artwork is written in a viewbox and mapped onto whatever size the element is. The same scene fits a 128 px console and a 760 px one, and stays sharp on both.
[h2]Getting started[/h2] Everything is in the mod folder ([i]Documents/My Games/Stationeers/mods/ScriptedScreensVector[/i]): [list] [*] [b]examples/[/b] -- fifteen numbered scripts that each run on paste, from a three-shape "hello" up to a complete four-tank gas console, scrolling lists, text, clicks and effects [*] [b]README.md[/b] -- the authoring guide: how a scene is structured, how it animates, and the traps [*] [b]REFERENCE.md[/b] -- every node, attribute and expression function [*] [b]Patterns.lua[/b] -- ready-made tanks, mote fields, dials, charts and alarm lamps [*] [b]CHANGELOG.md[/b] -- the full release history [*] [b]QUICKSTART.md[/b] -- a one-page brief with a working template and a checklist [/list] The same files are [url=https://github.com/Gruffuss/scripted-screens-vector/tree/main/ScriptedScreensVector]on GitHub[/url].
[h2]AI editor support (MCP)[/h2] With [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3659911735]StationeersLua[/url] installed, an AI editor connected to its MCP server gets everything it needs to write vector scenes: [list] [*] [b]stationeers://vector/index[/b] -- a brief written for AI: when to use the element, a template that runs as written, a checklist of the mistakes that fail silently, and a map of every other page [*] the guide and reference, one searchable page per section (search scope [b]vector[/b]), the changelog, Patterns.lua and all fifteen examples [*] [b]vector_stats[/b] -- a tool reporting every live scene's build, cost and problems, so the editor can check its own work alongside ScriptedScreens' capture tool [/list] Nothing changes without StationeersLua; the mod works the same.
[h2]Notes[/h2] [list] [*] A concave clip draws what it clips once per convex piece, so prefer convex outlines where the design allows [*] Text updates at the redraw rate rather than instantly, so a label element is still the better choice for something that must change the moment a value does [*] A broken scene says so: it draws a magenta border and names the fault, rather than looking switched off [*] Level of detail is automatic -- update rate and curve smoothness both follow on-screen size; consoles off screen or in a paused game cost nothing [*] Turn on Diagnostics in the settings to see exactly what a scene costs [/list]
[h2]Changelog[/h2] [b]0.11.25[/b] [list] [*] [b]MCP support for AI editors.[/b] With StationeersLua's MCP server, the mod publishes a brief written for AI editors (stationeers://vector/index), the guide and reference split into searchable sections (scope [b]vector[/b]), the changelog, Patterns.lua and all examples, next to the existing vector_stats tool. [*] QUICKSTART.md ships in the mod folder: the same one-page brief, with a working template and a checklist. [/list] [b]0.11.24[/b] [list] [*] Other mods on the same client can follow a scroll container's offset (ScrollChanged, TryGetScroll); with Diagnostics on, each change is logged. [*] Fixed: a script-set scroll jump (so, sov) landed short of its target while data was easing, e.g. at 149.1 instead of 150. [/list] [b]0.11.23[/b] [list] [*] Fixed: a path with a hole inside a clipped group drew solid. Clipped fills keep their holes, including one the clip cuts through or one crossing a concave clip's pieces. [/list] Older releases: [b]CHANGELOG.md[/b] in the mod folder, or [url=https://github.com/Gruffuss/scripted-screens-vector/blob/main/ScriptedScreensVector/CHANGELOG.md]on GitHub[/url].
